title: Suspected Chinese Hackers Turn VMware vCenter RCE Into Root Backdoors and ESXi Ransomware
content_md: A suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor has exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server vulnerability to gain root-level access, establish several backdoors, steal directory credentials, and deploy Babuk-derived ransomware on ESXi hypervisors. The campaign targeted CVE-2026-59310, a critical directory-traversal flaw in VMware vCenter’s Syslog Server that can allow remote code execution. Broadcom assigned the bug a CVSS score of 9.8 and disclosed it on July 29, 2026. Researchers observed the first compromised systems contacting attacker infrastructure on August 3 only five days later. Security firm QUIRSO identified 361 unique victim IP addresses across 47 countries. Germany, the United States, Turkey, Iran, and France were the most affected locations. The victims included technology firms, universities, research organizations, telecom companies, and network-service providers. The researchers cautioned that IP addresses do not directly equal the number of victim organizations, as some systems may belong to shared hosting or cloud environments. Chinese Actors Weaponize vCenter The attackers appear to have abused the vulnerable vCenter Syslog Server to write malicious content into /etc/cron.d/ , a directory used by Linux cron for scheduled task execution. A suspicious file named zz-poc59310-syslog.log referenced the CVE number and triggered a root-level command that downloaded and launched a payload called linuxFile .
